---
title: "Save predictions and resume interrupted training"
---

METIS has two deliberately different artifacts. An **inference artifact** is
for prediction in another process. A **training checkpoint** additionally
records the optimizer and random state needed to resume an interrupted job.

## Portable inference

```python
from metis import Surrogate
model.save("surrogate.pt")
restored = Surrogate.load("surrogate.pt", device="cpu")
predictions = restored.predict({"contact_rate": 0.4, "recovery_rate": 0.1})
```

Input names in this example must match your fitted schema. The artifact includes
weights, architecture, scalers, time grid and provenance. It needs no simulation
bank at prediction time. Calling `fit` starts a fitting operation; use the
explicit resume option below to continue an interrupted one.

## Training checkpoints

```bash
uv run metis train training.steps=10000 training.checkpoint_every=500 training.checkpoint_dir=/absolute/path/checkpoints/run-a
```

Replace `/absolute/path` with a real location. A relative Hydra checkpoint
directory lives under that job's output directory; a relative `resume_from` path
is resolved from the launch directory. Absolute paths remove this ambiguity.
The directory receives `last.pt` at the requested cadence and at completion,
and `best.pt` when validation selects better weights. To resume an interrupted
run, repeat the original data/model/training settings and add the checkpoint:

```bash
uv run metis train training.steps=10000 training.checkpoint_every=500 training.checkpoint_dir=/absolute/path/checkpoints/run-a training.resume_from=/absolute/path/checkpoints/run-a/last.pt
```

`steps` is the **original total**, not a count of additional steps. Resume
requires the original model, bank identities, schemas, scalers, optimizer,
schedule, seed, precision and device topology. Only checkpoint location,
cadence and resume path may change. METIS rejects incompatible continuation
rather than silently interpreting a checkpoint under a different experiment.

The same fields are available in `TrainingConfig` for Python. Training
checkpoints are not accepted by `Surrogate.load`; keep the inference artifact
saved after fitting for deployment. Pre-package raw checkpoints lack essential
preprocessing metadata: see [migration](../package/migration.qmd).
